title: Past Tense 4: Irregular Past Tense
description: Irregular past forms with no -л in the masculine: the -чь class (мог, лёг, пёк) and the -ти / -сти class (шёл, нёс, вёл). The feminine, neuter, and plural still take regular -ла / -ло / -ли endings.
descriptionRussian: Неправильные формы прошедшего времени без -л в мужском роде: класс на -чь (мог, лёг, пёк) и класс на -ти / -сти (шёл, нёс, вёл). Женский, средний и множественное числа сохраняют -ла / -ло / -ли.
intro: Two families of verbs drop the -л in the masculine and leave a bare stem behind. It looks alarming and is contained: only the masculine is affected, and the other three forms take the regular endings you already have. These are common verbs, though, including 'could', 'went' and 'carried', so you meet the odd form constantly.
rules: The -чь class (мочь, лечь, печь) has a masculine past with no -л: мог, лёг, пёк. The fem / neut / pl add regular -ла́ / -ло́ / -ли́ to the past stem.
The -ти / -сти class (идти, нести, вести) has a similar masculine past: шёл, нёс, вёл. The fem / neut / pl add the regular endings to the (sometimes vowel-shifted) stem.

The vowel alternation -ё- / -е- is stress-conditioned: -ё- under stress (always in the masc since the masc form has no ending), -е- unstressed in the rest. So нёс / несла́, лёг / легла́, пёк / пекла́. Идти is not part of this pattern: its feminine шла has no stem vowel at all.
The plural -ли and the neuter -ло in this family are end-stressed: могли́, легли́, пекли́, шли́, несли́, вели́; могло́, легло́, пекло́, шло́, несло́, вело́.
examples: Антон мог помочь. (Anton was able to help.) Мочь masc: мог.
Маша могла́ помочь. (Masha was able to help.) Мочь fem: могла́.
Мы могли́ помочь. (We were able to help.) Мочь pl: могли́.
Антон шёл домой. (Anton was walking home.) Идти masc: шёл (suppletive stem).
Маша шла́ домой. (Masha was walking home.) Идти fem: шла́.
Лена несла́ книгу. (Lena was carrying a book.) Нести fem: несла́, vowel -е- unstressed.

items.promptEnglish: Masha was at home all day.
items.hint: Recap from Lesson 2: быть, feminine subject, end-stressed была́.
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 2. Маша is feminine; the past of быть takes the feminine form, which is end-stressed: была́. Today's drill, starting Q1.2, switches to verbs whose masculine past has no -л.

items.promptEnglish: Anton was able to help. (Which masculine form is correctly built?)
items.hint: -чь class. The regular rule (drop -ть, add -л) does not apply to the masculine here.
items.explanation: Мочь is in the -чь class. The masc past has no -л: just the bare past stem мог. The fem / neut / pl do add the regular endings (могла́, могли́), but the masc does not.

items.promptEnglish: Masha was walking home. (Which form uses the correct past stem?)
items.hint: Идти uses a completely different root in the past, not ид-. Which root does it use?
items.explanation: Идти is irregular even within the -ти class: the past stem is ш-, a completely different root unrelated to ид-. The feminine is шла́.

items.promptEnglish: Lena was carrying a book to school. (Which feminine form has the correct stem vowel?)
items.hint: Stress moves to the ending in the feminine. What does the stem vowel do once it loses the stress?
items.explanation: Нести fem is несла́. The masc нёс carries -ё- because the whole form is just the stressed stem; once the ending takes the stress (fem -ла́), the stem vowel drops to -е-.

items.promptEnglish: Anton was leading the children to the park. (Which masculine form is correctly built?)
items.hint: Вести keeps -л in the masc but the stem vowel still alternates. Which form has -ё- AND just one -л?
items.explanation: Вести masc is вёл: -ё- under stress (since the stem carries the stress in the masc) and a single -л.

items.promptEnglish: The children were walking home. (Which plural form uses the correct past stem?)
items.hint: Идти uses a completely different root in the past. The plural is built from the same ш- root as the other past forms.
items.explanation: Идти plural is шли́, end-stressed, built on the ш- root (a completely different root, unrelated to ид-).

blanks: Маша _____ хлеб в духовке. (Masha was baking bread in the oven.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Печь fem is пекла́: same -чь-class pattern as мог / могла́. Stress moves to the ending in the feminine, so the stem vowel drops from -ё- (which only appears under stress, as in masc пёк) to -е-: пекла́.

minimalPairs.explanation: Антон is masculine, so the past of идти takes the masculine form шёл. Шла would be required for a feminine subject (Маша шла домой).

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Masha was carrying a book. (Pick the feminine form with the correct stem vowel.)
minimalPairs.explanation: Both options are feminine, so gender alone does not decide. The stress moves to the -ла́ ending in the feminine, so the stem vowel drops from -ё- to -е-: несла. Нёсла would keep the masculine's stressed -ё- next to a fem ending, but -ё- only appears under stress, so it cannot survive when the stress moves away.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Yesterday Anton went to bed early.
errorCorrection.explanation: The -чь-class masculine past has no -л: just the past stem лёг. Лёгл is the form a learner builds by mechanically dropping -ть and adding -л, exactly the regular rule the -чь class does not follow.
Маша is feminine, so the past of идти takes the feminine form шла. Шёл is the masculine form. The suppletive stem ш- is the same across all four slots; gender/number agreement decides the ending.

The fem form drops -ё- to -е-. Stress moves to the -ла́ ending, so the stem vowel drops to -е-: несла. Нёсла would mix the masc -ё- with the fem -ла, which is ungrammatical because -ё- only appears under stress.

The plural of идти is шли, not шёли. The plural -ли is end-stressed and the stem has no vowel here; only the masc form шёл carries the -ё-. The -ё- in идти's masc is a stressed-vowel relic; once the ending takes the stress, no vowel remains in the stem.

reviewVocab.definition: the -чь class (мочь, лечь, печь, помочь, all verbs whose infinitive ends in -чь and whose past masculine has no -л)
reviewVocab.example: Глагол 'мочь' принадлежит к классу на -чь: его прошедшее время — мог / могла́ / могло́ / могли́.

reviewVocab.definition: the -ти / -сти class (идти, нести, вести, all verbs whose infinitive ends in -ти or -сти and whose past masculine has no -л)
reviewVocab.example: Глагол 'нести' принадлежит к классу на -ти: его прошедшее — нёс / несла́ / несло́ / несли́.

reviewVocab.definition: alternation (the -ё- / -е- vowel switch conditioned by stress: stem-stressed -ё- in the masc, ending-stressed forms drop to -е-)
reviewVocab.example: В формах 'нёс / несла́' видно чередование -ё- / -е-: ударение перешло на окончание, и в основе появилось -е-.
